tool_input.title: aurora-lab shop/api rollout stuck - missing secret api-secrets
tool_input.content:
Incident: KubeDeploymentRolloutStuck, deployment `api` in namespace `shop`, cluster `aurora-lab` (kind-aurora-lab, cluster_id kubeconfig-d36c45afe6194d68), 2026-10-02.

Root cause: Deployment `api` was bumped to revision 2, adding a new mandatory env var `DB_PASSWORD` (valueFrom secretKeyRef: name=api-secrets, key=db-password, Optional:false) to the pod template. The Secret `api-secrets` was never created in the `shop` namespace (confirmed via `kubectl get secrets -A` — it doesn't exist anywhere in the cluster, only kube-system/bootstrap-token exists). New ReplicaSet pods fail with `CreateContainerConfigError` / `Error: secret "api-secrets" not found`, so the rollout stalls at N-1 updated replicas while the old ReplicaSet keeps serving traffic (no outage, Available=True).

Notably: the actual app code (`api.py` in configmap `api-code`) only reads `REDIS_HOST` — it does NOT use `DB_PASSWORD` at all. The env var was added to the manifest ahead of any code that consumes it (premature/accidental infra change), so this is a pure manifest/config drift issue, not a legitimate app dependency breaking.

**Why this matters:** This pattern (deployment manifest references a Secret/ConfigMap key that doesn't exist, especially when added without being tied to a code change) causes classic "rollout stuck, new pods not starting" alerts in this lab cluster. The namespace `shop` on cluster aurora-lab hosts: api (python:3.12-alpine, depends on redis + api-secrets), frontend (nginx), worker (python, batch processing, high memory per batch), redis, loadgen (busybox traffic generator).

**How to apply:** On KubeDeploymentRolloutStuck for shop/api or similar, immediately check `kubectl describe pod <new-pod>` for Waiting reason, cross-check `kubectl get secrets -n <ns>` and `kubectl get secrets -A` to see if a referenced secret/configmap is simply missing, and diff env vars between old (still-Running) ReplicaSet pods and the new one to spot what changed. Also check whether the actual app code in the mounted ConfigMap actually uses the new env var — if not, the env var addition itself may be the mistake rather than a legitimate requirement needing a real secret value.
